unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 12 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.4 - THEME 4: FAMILY LIFE & HOME

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will work on the theme of family life and home by focusing on the sub-themes of maintaining relationships with family members and the challenges that modern societies present for families. They will design a presentation (either as a video, slideshow, or written report) that focuses on the importance of staying connected with family members despite busy lives and geographical distances. In their project, they are asked to discuss some of the challenges families face today and the effects of modern technology on family bonding. They can enrich their projects with personal examples or interviews with family members to illustrate these challenges. Finally, they will propose creative solutions or strategies for overcoming these challenges. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''family life and home with its components such as maintaining relationship with family members; challenges of modern societies for families'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in after prep year 12 of upper secondary school may know what maintaining relationship with family members; challenges of modern societies for families mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in after prep year 12 of upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''family life and home'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year, and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in after prep year 12 of upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''family life and home with its components such as maintaining relationship with family members; challenges of modern societies for families'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To analyse family challenges in modern societies and find solutions in English by using critical thinking and the target vocabulary Activity Name: Fishbone Diagram: Family Challenges and Solutions Students create a fishbone diagram with the topic ''Challenges and Solutions of Modern Societies for Families'' at its heading. On the left side, labelled ''Challenges'', they list issues such as financial instability, isolation, and family conflicts. On the right side: ''Solutions'', they propose practical ideas like holding family meetings, seeking community support, and implementing effective budgeting strategies. When the diagrams are completed, students present their work to the class by explaining their identified challenges and proposed solutions. Following the presentations, the class engages in a reflective discussion, comparing the challenges and solutions shared. They consider questions such as: ''Do you experience similar challenges in your family?'', and ''Which solutions do you think would be most effective in your situation?''. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about maintaining relationships with family members and challenges of modern societies for families in English by using the target vocabulary and language items. Activity: Family Tree Report The teacher asks students to design a simple fictional family tree featuring 2–4 members. For each family member, students write two or three sentences by using the target language to describe their relationships and roles within the family. Students then work in pairs to exchange information about their fictional family trees. After the pair work, each student reports to the class about their peer's family using the target language. The teacher provides constructive and encouraging feedback, focusing on the use of language, accuracy and creativity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
